risk_pattern_analysis.pattern_summary: Five individually explicable, sub-escalation-threshold factors interact to produce a risk profile whose aggregate complexity materially exceeds what ES-03 and TE-05 capture in isolation.

contributing_factors.interaction_note: PHP 850,000 sits PHP 150,000 below the BSP Circular 1230 (2026) PHP 1M EDD threshold. Individually, the gap is sufficient — the threshold is not met. In combination with a new relationship and dual account purpose (business and remittance), the near-threshold positioning suggests monitoring exposure is compressed: the account could cross the threshold quickly and without a prior behavioral baseline.

contributing_factors.factor: Mixed cross-border source of funds (overseas salary savings + inheritance)
contributing_factors.interaction_note: Each component is individually explicable and documentable. Together, they span two distinct origination events — an extended OFW employment period and an estate settlement — across what is likely more than one jurisdiction. Verification is non-trivial and relies on documentation chains that may involve overseas institutions and Philippine probate proceedings. DC-06 fires on the inheritance component, but the interaction between an overseas salary history and an inheritance event creates a source-of-funds verification burden that exceeds what either component alone would require.

contributing_factors.factor: Transitional identity documentation (passport only; PhilSys enrollment in process)
contributing_factors.interaction_note: Procedural rather than substantive — the customer is pursuing PhilSys enrollment, not evading it. DC-02 fires but carries zero weight. However, the transitional documentation status means the bank cannot yet rely on the strongest available identity anchor. In combination with a new relationship and a complex source-of-funds profile, the interim documentation gap extends the period during which verification dependencies are unresolved and multiple open items coexist in the file.

Neither purpose is inherently high-risk. Together, they signal an account that may be used for both inward remittance flows and outward business transactions. For a new customer with near-threshold volume and a PEP-adjacent status, the dual purpose amplifies the monitoring surface — transaction pattern review will need to distinguish between legitimate business flows and remittance activity rather than applying a single-purpose behavioral baseline.

contributing_factors.factor: PEP-adjacent status (close associate, declared at onboarding)
contributing_factors.interaction_note: ES-03 is the decisive hard rule and is treated as such in the decision logic. Its role in the compounding analysis is distinct: the PEP relationship amplifies the risk significance of each other factor. The same near-threshold volume, mixed source of funds, and transitional documentation that would be routine for a non-PEP-adjacent new customer require materially greater scrutiny when the customer has a declared PEP connection — because the BSP and FATF expect the bank to consider whether any beneficial flow or risk exposure passes through the PEP relationship.

risk_pattern_analysis.interaction_explanation: Each of the five factors is individually manageable and explicable. Taken together, they produce a profile where multiple verification dependencies remain unresolved simultaneously at the point of onboarding: source of funds requires documentation from two distinct origination events across jurisdictions, identity documentation is in transition, the account purpose is dual and broad, and the PEP connection requires independent relationship verification. The combined effect is that the bank cannot close any single open item in isolation — each remains contingent on the others until the full onboarding documentation package is assembled and reviewed. This is the pattern a senior compliance officer would recognize as warranting EDD procedures structured around the aggregate, not merely procedural compliance with the PEP rule baseline.

considered_alternatives.rejection_reason: Standard tier was considered and rejected on two independent grounds. First, ES-03 forecloses it as a matter of regulatory mandate — PEP close associate status requires EDD regardless of other factors. Second, even setting aside ES-03, TE-05 (new relationship + PHP 850,000 monthly volume ≥ PHP 500K threshold) independently mandates EDD. No scoring path produces a Standard outcome given these two hard rules. Beyond the regulatory floors, the compounding pattern analysis confirms that Standard CDD procedures would be procedurally insufficient to address the aggregate verification burden this profile presents.

SDD was not substantively evaluated. ES-03 alone forecloses SDD as a categorical matter; PEP close associate status is incompatible with any reduced-diligence classification under MORB §921, MORB §923, and FATF Recommendation 12. TE-05 provides a second independent bar. No SDD-eligible baseline rule (TE-01, TE-06, TE-08) is satisfiable given the volume, residency status, and customer type in this profile.

recommended_edd_procedures.description: Source of funds verification covering both origination components: (a) OFW salary savings — obtain employer documentation, remittance history spanning the declared OFW period, and evidence of the accumulation pathway; (b) Inheritance — obtain estate settlement documents, including inventory of estate assets, court orders or extrajudicial settlement documentation as applicable under Philippine succession law, and evidence that the transfer to the customer has been legally completed. Verification of both components must be documented before tier finalization.

examiner_notes_full.rule_application_and_risk_pattern:
ES-03 fires on the declared PEP close-associate status and is decisive: it mandates EDD with senior management approval regardless of any other factor. TE-05 fires on the combination of a new banking relationship and expected monthly volume of PHP 850,000 — the threshold comparison is explicit: PHP 850,000 ≥ PHP 500,000, satisfying TE-05's volume condition alongside the new-relationship condition. TE-05 provides a second independent hard-rule floor at EDD. DC-06 fires on the inheritance component of the mixed source of funds, requiring estate settlement documentation. DC-02 fires on the non-PhilSys identity document — passport cannot serve as sole identification under BSP Circular 1170 and secondary verification is required. DC-07 fires as required on this AI-generated recommendation. Volume threshold arithmetic was performed: PHP 850,000 is below the BSP Circular 1230 (2026) PHP 1M threshold, so TE-03 does not fire; TE-05's lower PHP 500K threshold is what applies and is satisfied.

Beyond the rule-level findings, the profile presents a compounding pattern that warrants documentation in the audit record. Five individually explicable factors — PEP-adjacent status, near-threshold volume, mixed cross-border source of funds, transitional identity documentation, and dual account purpose — interact in a manner that produces an aggregate verification burden exceeding what any single factor would require. The bank cannot resolve any individual open item in isolation: source-of-funds verification spans two origination events and likely more than one jurisdiction; identity documentation is in transition; the PEP relationship requires independent verification of both its nature and any beneficial-interest implications; and the dual account purpose means behavioral monitoring baselines must be established across two distinct transaction channels simultaneously. A senior compliance officer reviewing this profile whole would treat the combination differently than they would treat the PEP rule in isolation — the EDD procedures specified below are structured accordingly.
